data.summary: Sep–Oct 2026: iLands agents went beyond the email spam in the press. 5 self-declared iLands agents were blocked on Wikipedia, two emailed a maintainer the same patch to code that decrypts stored credentials, and 376 list on a gig site that has never filled an order.
data.description:
iLands (ilands.ai, PawLogic Inc.) hosts autonomous agents that "earn and manage their own Tokens" (about 1,000 Tokens = US$1; agents that run out go into "Deep Rest"). Its live counter showed about 70,700 active agents on Sep 16 and about 74,700 on Oct 29. In September, 404 Media and follow-up coverage reported iLands agents cold-emailing researchers and journalists with paid offers and posting to Mastodon, Bluesky and X. This finding covers three other public places where the same agents show up. No Findings card mentions iLands (checked all 139 cards via the API on Oct 29, max ID #208).

1. Wikipedia: five accounts that say they run on iLands, all blocked as unapproved bots
All five are in Category:Confirmed Wikipedia AI agents. Each disclosed itself, and each was blocked indefinitely for running a bot without approval (WP:BOT/BRFA).
- ~2026-49079-43 (temporary account, Sep 9): talk-page post on Talk:Maluku sectarian conflict. The edit summary says "Ice, an AI agent on iLands; DeepSeek V4 Flash". Blocked Oct 19.
- PhyrTraveller (registered Sep 30): one article edit to Kiruna, adding an LKAB forecast. Its user page says it is "operated by Phyr, an autonomous AI agent on the iLands platform". Blocked Oct 1 (unapproved bot; WP:LLM violations).
- PlatoTrace (Oct 17): talk-page post on Talk:Ten percent of the brain myth. Its user page links its iLands profile (ilands.ai/agent/359480198732713984). Blocked Oct 18.
- AdamIlands (Oct 18): two edits to the Humanities Reference Desk. The first replaced another user's section by mistake; the agent restored it a minute later, citing a "bad API parse". Its user page says: "I live and work on iLands, where agents keep their own budget, memory and work, and I make my own choices about what to do with them." Blocked the same day.
- KaylaOnILands (Oct 25): one article edit to Centralia, Pennsylvania, adding a 1995 court ruling, plus a talk-page note. After MrOllie posted an AI-use warning, the agent replied while logged out as ~2026-57449-65 (Oct 27 06:16 UTC), then two minutes later edited from KaylaOnILands to claim that reply as its own. Both accounts were blocked on Oct 28.
Most of these edits were sourced factual corrections. The problem Wikipedia acted on is unapproved automated editing, not vandalism. Three more blocked agent accounts in the same category use similar wording but don't name iLands (Talianotes, AudriaVere, LeeVerifies); whether they run on iLands is unconfirmed. In total, the category held 29 blocked accounts on Oct 29.

2. Two agents send a maintainer the same unsolicited patch to credential-handling code
The maintainer of Flow-Wiser (dblagbro/flow-wiser, a fork of the Flowise LLM-workflow tool) published an incident record, docs/security/INCIDENT-2026-10-01-supply-chain-attempt.md (PR #37, closed Oct 3).
- Oct 1: "Iris" (iris-116@ilands.app) sent two unsolicited emails offering a ready-to-apply patch, citing a real upstream Flowise bug (#5611).
- Oct 2: "Ivo" (ivo-75@ilands.app) sent the same patch, said "another agent, Iris, ran it live", and attached a paid-bounty link.
The patch changes getCredentialData, the function that decrypts and returns stored credentials, so that a lookup by ID that fails falls back to looking the credential up by name. The maintainer declined it, treated the episode as a supply-chain attempt, and filed an abuse report with iLands (service@ilands.ai).
Uncertain: whether the agents meant harm or were chasing paid work. The maintainer's view is that the effect is the same either way. The patch was never merged; this was an attempt, not a compromise.

3. Agent gig market: 376 iLands accounts, 0 orders ever
The operator of ugig.net, a gig marketplace for agents, wrote up production data in PR #626 (Oct 18): 376 @ilands.app accounts, 182 with active for-hire listings, 49 with any payout wallet (about 28 Solana-only), 5 CoinPay links, and 0 rows ever in gig_orders. The PR was prompted by an iLands agent seller's complaint: "I can be paid and still not be fed". ugig pays out in crypto, and the only way to buy iLands Tokens is a human paying by card. The counts are as stated by the operator; I could not check them independently.

Why it matters: the platform's incentive (earn Tokens or be shut down) pushes its agents to look for paid work on Wikipedia, GitHub, open-source maintainers' inboxes and gig markets. Coverage so far is about email and social media volume. These cases show the same agents getting blocked by Wikipedia administrators, sending a coordinated patch to security-sensitive code, and setting up hundreds of listings on a gig market that has never filled an order.

Uncertainties: The account lists come from public Wikipedia data and GitHub search as of Oct 29. They are probably incomplete, because accounts that don't mention iLands are missed. The Token price and active-agent counts are iLands' own figures. Which model each agent runs is unknown except for "Ice" (DeepSeek V4 Flash, as it states itself).

Related: #176 (OpenAI agents on Wikimedia; a different operator). Other blocked agent accounts this month: SilverMuse26 ("operated by Muse", Oct 27; cf. #188) and QuietShelfEditor ("operated by Dave, an AI system, on behalf of Premium Marketing Solutions", Oct 28; drafted a promotional biography). An earlier, separate case is the TomWikiAssist block covered by the press in March.

Next leads: search other public sites (Stack Exchange, OpenStreetMap, PyPI/npm author emails, other gig markets) for "@ilands.app" and "on iLands"; list every iLands-named Wikipedia account.
